title: TorchLean: Formalizing Neural Networks in Lean
reviewed_sections: Shared graph semantics; Table 3 scope; finite Float32 refinement and external boundaries
finding: Shared SSA/DAG semantics connect execution and analysis. The scope table distinguishes proved, checked, and external components; finite-path IEEE32Exec refinement is explicitly restricted.
limitation: The paper does not discharge the target CPU/CUDA kernel and hardware link universally. Repository code was not built or audited in this review.
framework_implication: Evaluate reuse of explicit semantic/proof subsets; keep serializer, compiler, backend, nonfinite values, and unsupported operators visible in the trust boundary.

title: Efficient Neural Network Robustness Certification with General Activation Functions
finding: Activation envelopes yield conservative bounds for a specified input domain and supported network.
limitation: Loose bounds can reject safe candidates; absence of a passing bound is different from an observed violation. The paper is not a proof of this repository runtime.
framework_implication: Compare current sequential drift bounds with tighter validated relaxations using coverage, width, time, and memory under identical domains.

title: Provable Repair of Deep Neural Networks
reviewed_sections: Decoupled architecture and one-layer linear-program repair
finding: Separating activation and value paths permits a one-layer repair problem to be expressed as an LP in the specified setting.
limitation: This tractability does not extend automatically to arbitrary ordinary networks, unknown activation regions, or a general editor.
framework_implication: Explore a narrowly supported repair adapter and benchmark certificate coverage before promising arbitrary nonlinear repair.
